A statistic has been doing the rounds regarding Ruben Amorim’s league record with AC Milan, which is gathering some attention.

His style of play is open to criticism, his selections are controversial, his words are regularly quite strong and he’s often called into question at the first sign of failure. For Amorim, his first months with the Rossoneri have been a rollercoaster ride.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There have been ups and downs: things have been better domestically, culminating in a derby victory over Inter, but in the Europa League the one win from four games means the Rossoneri at the moment sit outside the playoff zone.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, there is a key bit of data to contextualise things. With 24 points in his first 11 Serie A matches, Amorim is averaging 2.18 points per game, the result of seven wins, three draws, and one defeat.

According to recent reports, it is the highest ever for a Milan coach in the three-point era, ahead of Stefano Pioli, Carlo Ancelotti and Massimiliano Allegri. Looking at coaches with at least five stints in the Italian top flight, only Antonio Conte boasts a better figure than the Portuguese coach, with 2.21 points per game.

This is obviously an unfair comparison, given that the former Napoli coach’s points average takes into account all 279 of his Serie A games – with spells at Atalanta, Juventus, Inter and Napoli – compared to just 11 for the former United manager.

However, it is a testament to the excellent work done thus far by Amorim and his staff. Even more so in a season in which the decision was made to undertake a revolution in several respects, to relaunch a team and a fan base that had been burned by the collapse of last season.

Gerry Cardinale and the ownership made significant investments during the last transfer window, spending €70m on Goncalo Ramos and €50m on Diego Moreira, plus €25m on Mario Gila. This is also why Milan fans have high expectations for Amorim’s era.

To date, the average from these first 11 games project the Rossoneri to land around 83 points by the end of the season. Last year, Inter won the Scudetto with 87 points, and 71 were needed to finish fourth, the minimum target set by the owners.

Allegri’s Milan stopped at 70 points, despite a strong start to the season that even fuelled a few Scudetto dreams for a few months. That start, however, was inferior to this season: a year ago, after 11 matchdays, AC Milan had 22 points, two fewer than under Amorim.

It is an encouraging beginning to the newly introduced era that fans hope will translate into concrete results, perhaps even the Scudetto, a target announced by owner Cardinale as a real aim, as unrealistic as it may have seemed before a ball was kicked.

Recent findings suggest that amorim is trying to convey his vision of football and instil a more European mentality in his team, and the numbers so far – at least in the league – seem to prove him right. To find a better start to a season one must rewind to 2022-23, when Milan had 26 points from 11 games under Pioli.

Ruben Amorim has the highest points-per-game average of any #ACMilan coach in Serie A in the three-points-per-win era: 2.18 over 11 matches.

Among all coaches with 5+ stints in the league during that period, only Antonio Conte (2.21) has a higher average.

[via @OptaPaolo] pic.twitter.com/jwPLgVw0z7.

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 19, 2026.

Speaking of Pioli, in the specific ranking of Milan coaches with the highest points average – led by Amorim, as mentioned – the coach who led the Rossoneri to their 19th Scudetto (2021-22) occupies second place at 2.02 points per game in 183 Serie A matches.

Pioli also achieved the best start in Milan’s history: in the Scudetto year, he earned 31 points from the opening 11 games, the result of 10 wins and 1 draw, with a record average of 2.82 points per game.

In third place among Milan coaches with the highest points average is Ancelotti, with 1.95 points in 283 Serie A games as Milan coach. Allegri is just off the podium, with 1.91 points in 172 games across his two spells at the club.

To compare Amorim with two of his compatriots who recently worked at Milanello, Paulo Fonseca averaged just 1.59 points per game from 17 games, while Sergio Conceicao fared slightly better with 1.71 points in 21 games.

Recent findings suggest that in short, Amorim’s performance is encouraging, but still relative given the very limited sample size. A crucial month is now beginning for Milan: a seven-game tour de force before Christmas that will reveal a lot about the true ambitions of the coach and his team, with form in Europe to fix.

Manchester United will be managed by Mauricio Pochettino for the first time as they face fierce rivals Liverpool this weekend.

The Argentine was appointed as Michael Carrick’s successor last week and only arrived in the UK on Wednesday, leaving him just a handful of sessions to prepare his Man Utd side for a crunch fixture at Anfield.

Industry observers note that as such, wholesale changes from life under Carrick are not forecast, at least in terms of setup. After all, both managers have a penchant for the same 4-2-3-1 formation.

Carlos Baleba remains sidelined with a hamstring injury sustained against Roma in the Champions League, with Benjamin Sesko also out until the Fresh Year, but Pochettino may well be boosted by the returns of Marcus Rashford and Luke Shaw.

The latter seems the more likely of the two to be available on Sunday, with Rashford yet to be pictured in training since the international break.

Pochettino is known to be fond of Rashford, and has reportedly attempted to sign him for other clubs he has managed, meaning he can expect to get the nod if fit.

Should Shaw slot in at left-back, he may do so as one of two fresh faces in the defence. Lisandro Martinez has served his red card suspension and will be available to partner Harry Maguire, with Diogo Dalot likely at right-back.

A midfield pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo should sit behind the trio of Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo, with Bryan Mbeumo leading the line.

Patrick Dorgu is expected to be available, but it remains to be seen whether he can unseat Cunha on the left flank. He could also deputise for Shaw if the latter is not fit enough to start.

Leaked drone footage of United’s Thursday training session appeared to show Pochettino working on tactics with a tight-knit group of 10 outfield players, leading some to speculate that he might be dealing with Sunday’s starters.

The presence of Joshua Zirkzee and Harry Amass in the group rather debunks that theory, though, given that neither player has started a Premier League match so far this season.

Doubts: Rashford, Shaw, Heaven, Darlow.

Breaking: Sparta Rotterdam vs AZ Alkmaar - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adepoju Marvellous | 20 Nov 2026 20:54, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:58.
  • A struggling Sparta Rotterdam outfit will set out in search of a return to winning ways in Sunday’s Eredivisie clash against AZ Alkmaar at Het Kasteel.
  • The visitors, meanwhile, travel to Rotterdam aiming for back-to-back wins for the first time since September, having snapped a three-game losing streak just before the international break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 20 Nov 2026 20:54, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:58.

A struggling Sparta Rotterdam outfit will set out in search of a return to winning ways in Sunday’s Eredivisie clash against AZ Alkmaar at Het Kasteel.

The visitors, meanwhile, travel to Rotterdam aiming for back-to-back wins for the first time since September, having snapped a three-game losing streak just before the international break.

AZ Alkmaar started the season with six wins and a draw from their opening seven Eredivisie matches, looking like the team to beat, but a 2-0 defeat to Feyenoord after the September break sparked a four-game winless run (D1, L3).

In arguably the game of the season so far, Leeroy Echteld’s men scored three times in the final 30 minutes of their most recent clash against Groningen to secure a 4-3 victory and keep themselves within three points of PSV Eindhoven at the top of the Eredivisie table.

De Kaasboeren have failed to win any of their league matches immediately preceding a Europa League group-stage fixture so far, and with a trip to Sparta Prague to follow this weekend, they will be eager to buck that trend of faltering domestically before continental duties.

AZ won both league meetings with Sparta last season, making it four wins from the last six encounters (D1, L1). Sunday’s visitors are also unbeaten in their last six trips to Het Kasteel, averaging two goals per game in that stretch.

However, AZ have struggled away from home recently, collecting just one point from the last nine available on their travels, which came in a 2-2 draw at Cambuur courtesy of a Mexx Merdink penalty seven minutes from time.

While not their heaviest, Sparta’s 3-1 defeat to newly-promoted ADO Den Haag was arguably their most disappointing loss of the 2026-27 season so far, especially given the momentum they carried into the clash after a thrilling 3-2 triumph over Groningen.

Rogier Meijer has now lost more than half of his 13 matches since taking charge in July, and pressure is beginning to mount on the 45-year-old.

Nevertheless, his experience at this level - having recently surpassed 200 matches as a manager in Dutch football - suggests he will be given time to turn things around.

Starting this weekend’s clash just two points clear of the drop zone, De Rood-Witte Gladiatoren risk ending matchday 13 inside the relegation places - a significant fall from grace for a side tipped to compete for Europe at the start of the campaign.

Only Utrecht and Willem II have conceded more goals than Sparta’s 29, and they are also one of five teams without a clean sheet, leaving little mystery about their biggest shortcoming this season.

Averaging 1.8 goals per game so far, Sunday’s hosts have fared reasonably well in attack, but an overreliance on Milan Zonneveld, who has been directly involved in nine of their 21 goals, can sometimes prove detrimental.

Sparta Rotterdam Eredivisie form:.

Sparta Rotterdam form (all competitions):.

AZ Alkmaar form (all competitions):.

Goalkeeper Michael Brouwer is Sparta’s only injury concern for Sunday’s clash after he was forced off late in the defeat to ADO Den Haag.

Filip Bednarek replaced Brouwer off the bench last time out and is ready to deputise in goal again if required.

Lushendry Martes will need to keep his discipline in check, having already collected four yellow cards this season, as one more would trigger a one-match suspension.

Jizz Hornkamp has made just three appearances this season and remains unavailable for AZ, as do fellow Dutchmen Stije Resink and Jeroen Zoet, who are both yet to feature in 2026-27.

Lewis Schouten’s involvement this weekend is right now in doubt after he was absent from the win over Groningen.

Twenty-three-year-old Mexx Meerdink has six goals and an assist in his last seven club matches and will be expected to deliver once again.

Sparta Rotterdam possible starting lineup:.

Bednarek; Martes, Young, Verschuren, Martins Indi, Kuipers; Van Bergen, Quintero, Hatenboer, Babadi; Zonneveld.

AZ Alkmaar possible starting lineup:.

De Busser; Chavez, Hoedt, Goes, Dijkstra; Koopmeiners, Kwakman; Daal, Byskov, Oufkir; Meerdink.

While Sparta’s defensive challenges need no introduction, AZ have also struggled at the back recently, so a clean sheet for either side seems unlikely.

That mentioned, Echteld’s men are strong favourites to get the job done, and we expect them to do so with relative ease.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Barcelona have confirmed they have no plans to sell Alejandro Balde and insist the Manchester United-linked left-back remains an ‘important player’ for the club going forward.

Balde has been with Barca since the age of just eight, making a total of 173 appearances in all competitions since breaking into the first-team squad back in 2021.

In that time, the 23-year-old has helped the Catalan giants win seven pieces of silverware, including three La Liga titles – the most recent coming under Hansi Flick last season.

However, Balde has become an increasingly peripheral figure at the Camp Nou in recent months, with all five of his appearances this term coming from the substitutes bench.

Balde right now finds himself behind both Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart in the pecking order at Barca and the Spain international’s career appears to be at a crossroads.

According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, this has forced Balde to consider his options and the full-back is understood to be keen on joining Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United in January.

Other reports suggest that ‘everything Balde has heard about his situation has come through press conferences’ and the defender views the Premier League as a possible escape route.

The subject of Balde’s future has proven a major talking point both in the media and amongst Barcelona’s fanbase – and the topic was raised during Catalunya Radio’s joint interview with club chiefs Bojan and Deco on Wednesday.

Asked about the possible sale of Balde this winter, football coordinator Bojan replied: ‘Balde is a fantastic lad.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

In a recent development, ‘Obviously, he’s in an uncomfortable situation. The player wants to play.

‘He’s one of our own and he’s still an notable player. It’s true that he’s not playing right now, although he’s ready if the manager needs him.’.

Deco, Barca’s sporting director, was similarly unequivocal when asked if a transfer deal could be on the cards for Balde.

‘No,’ the ex-Barca, Chelsea and Portugal responded.

‘There is also the player’s side, but he hasn’t told us anything about being unhappy, that’s not the case.’.

Manchester United had been actively looking to strengthen at left-back in the summer in order to provide support and competition for Luke Shaw, the club’s only specialist in the position other than academy product Harry Amass.

The Red Devils ultimately failed to bolster their full-back options, though, which has come back to bite them already this season, with Shaw sidelined for the last month through injury.

Diogo Dalot was therefore forced to fill in as a makeshift left-back in the bleak final weeks of Michael Carrick’s tenure at the Theatre of Dreams.

It’s understood Lewis Hall had been identified as United’s number one left-back target ahead of the 2026/27 campaign, but Newcastle made it clear the England international would not be sold for anything other than an astronomical price.

Hall would go on to put pen to paper on a new long-term deal at St James’ Park, tying him to the Magpies until 2031.

Bournemouth’s Adrien Truffert, Fulham’s Antonee Robinson, RB Leipzig’s David Raum and Crystal Palace’s Tyrick Mitchell have also been linked in recent months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Barcelona have Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez on their transfer shortlist ahead of the January window, according to reports.

Martinez is into his fifth season at United after signing from Ajax for £57million in 2022.

The Argentine has made 121 appearances in all competitions for the Red Devils, but is out of contract at the end of the season.

United do have the option to trigger a 12-month extension to Martinez’s contract, but they may have reservations after he released a scathing public critique of the club’s transfer strategy last month.

And now, Mundo Deportivo reports that Barcelona could be waiting in the wings to pounce as they seek to add a centre-back in the January window.

Inter Milan stalwart Alessandro Bastoni and Borussia Dortmund defender Nico Schlotterbeck are also being considered by the Catalalan giants as options to strengthen Hansi Flick’s side.

But Martinez is viewed as the ‘most economical’ alternative, with the Barca keen on his experience and capability to operate on the left side of defence.

The report adds that Martinez would be willing to listen to an offer, although the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino as United’s newly introduced manager could complicate Barcelona’s pursuit.

Pochettino will take charge of his first match against Liverpool on Sunday, but former Red Devils defender Gary Neville expects Martinez will be one of several defenders to make way in the coming transfer windows.

‘And then the year after you’d be looking at Shaw, Maguire, Dalot, Bruno, that’s your second wave and maybe then you’ve made your mind up on Baleba and Santos.

‘But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.’.

Liverpool face rivals Manchester United in the Premier League on Sunday with a strong squad available.

Reds boss Andoni Iraola had plenty of good news to deliver at his pre-match press conference on Friday, as he confirmed that Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong - all previously considered doubts - would be fit to feature at Anfield.

All three missed out on international duty with the Netherlands - Van Dijk pulling out of the squad after concerns over a ‘little niggle’ he has been carrying of late.

In a recent development, dominik Szoboszlai has also struggled with fitness in recent weeks, but came through two games for Hungary unscathed. Iraola will also have been pleased with Alexander Isak being rested for Sweden’s second game of the international window, leaving Liverpool’s top scorer in top condition for the weekend.

It has been revealed that alisson will start in goal, while Van Dijk should continue his strong centre-back partnership with Jeremy Jacquet. Milos Kerkez is first-choice at left-back, but injuries at right-back have caused Iraola headaches all season.

Ronald Araujo has deputised on the right for the majority of the season, and he will likely start there again on Sunday.

A fully fit Szoboszlai is Liverpool’s best midfielder, so the Hungarian is slated to start alongside Alexis Mac Allister - now just one yellow card away from a suspension - in the engine room against United.

Florian Wirtz saw his best run of form since signing for the club last summer interrupted slightly by injury, but the German should soon get back into a rhythm with another start at No10.

Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo should start out wide, with Isak leading the line. Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni are both now back in training but won’t return here, while fellow long-term absentee Hugo Ekitike is expected to play again in January.

Predicted Liverpool XI vs Man Utd (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araujo, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister; Barcola, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak.

#83847. Nico Paz compared to Messi and Maradona amid Real Madrid return rumours

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (905 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Nico Paz compared to Messi and Maradona amid Real Madrid return rumours

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (905 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 20:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:01.
  • Real Madrid's reported looks to bring Nico Paz back to the Santiago Bernabeu for £68m have attracted fresh attention after former Manchester United and Chelsea midfielder Juan Sebastian Veron compared the Argentine youngster's abilities to those of Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona.
  • Los Blancos are reportedly preparing to activate their €80m (£68m) buy-back option for the Como playmaker next summer, having watched his remarkable development under Cesc Fabregas in Serie A.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 20:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:01.

Real Madrid's reported looks to bring Nico Paz back to the Santiago Bernabeu for £68m have attracted fresh attention after former Manchester United and Chelsea midfielder Juan Sebastian Veron compared the Argentine youngster's abilities to those of Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona.

Los Blancos are reportedly preparing to activate their €80m (£68m) buy-back option for the Como playmaker next summer, having watched his remarkable development under Cesc Fabregas in Serie A.

According to Spanish radio station COPE, Madrid have decided to exercise the clause, which can only be triggered during the summer 2027 transfer window.

The 22-year-old has scored six goals and provided eight assists in 14 club appearances this season, establishing himself as one of the most influential attacking midfielders in Italian football.

However, Veron's latest assessment of Paz offers more than an extraordinary comparison with two of Argentina's greatest players.

The former Argentina international has also emphasised the importance of regular football in developing young talents, a consideration that could become significant if Paz returns to a Madrid squad already containing Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler.

Speaking in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport, Veron reserved exceptional praise for Paz after the midfielder continued his impressive international development.

"Nico Paz has incredible talent. He is destined for great things," the former Manchester United midfielder noted. "The future belongs to him if he continues to behave like a professional, as he is doing.".

Industry observers note that veron then made a particularly striking comparison. "At 22, I have only seen Messi and a certain Diego Armando Maradona do certain things like that.".

In a recent development, the 51-year-old was careful not to suggest that Paz was guaranteed to reach the extraordinary heights achieved by either legend. "I don't mean that he will reach those levels, but he has the qualities to attempt it," Veron explained.

What particularly impresses the former Chelsea midfielder is the confidence Paz displays when receiving possession under pressure.

Veron highlighted the youngster's ability to dictate the rhythm of attacks, move into dangerous positions and retain the trust of his teammates even when closely marked.

Rather than describing him solely as an individual talent, he identified Paz as the player around whom Como organise much of their attacking football.

Recent findings suggest that "Nico is a leader in the way he manages moves. He is the focal point of the game," Veron added.

Those qualities have become increasingly apparent under Fabregas, whose possession-based approach has allowed the Argentine to develop into a central figure.

In a recent development, paz has also carried his club form onto the international stage. He recently scored twice for Argentina against Costa Rica, further strengthening his credentials as one of the country's leading young talents following Messi's international retirement.

His performances have inevitably increased speculation surrounding his next move, with Madrid retaining a significant advantage over other potential suitors.

Paz left Madrid for Como in the summer of 2024, having made only eight senior appearances for the Spanish giants.

His move to Italy initially offered an opportunity to gain regular first-team experience, but the relationship between the two clubs has since become more complicated.

During the summer of 2026, Como reportedly paid an additional €60m to acquire full ownership of the player, while Madrid retained a final buy-back option worth €80m.

That clause is valid for the summer of 2027, meaning Madrid have a limited opportunity to bring their former academy player back on preferential terms.

COPE now reports that the Spanish giants intend to exercise that option, although the deal has not been officially completed.

As previously reported by Sports Mole, Madrid face an vital decision over Paz's future, particularly because of the attacking competition awaiting him at the Bernabeu.

Bellingham has established himself as a key figure in Madrid's midfield, while Guler has also become increasingly influential under Jose Mourinho.

Recent findings suggest that the club possesses several other attacking options, including Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Yan Diomande. Consequently, there is no guarantee that Paz would enjoy the same importance in Madrid's starting XI that he currently possesses at Como.

Veron's comments about another young Argentine, Franco Mastantuono, offer an interesting perspective on that challenge.

Discussing the youngster's development during his loan spell at Fiorentina, Veron argued that consistent opportunities were essential for establishing himself at the highest level.

According to recent reports, "Nico Paz became a leader at Como by playing," he explained. "I have never known a player who became a team leader by sitting on the bench.".

Veron was discussing the benefits of regular football rather than explicitly warning Paz against returning to Madrid. Nevertheless, his observations underline an key consideration for the Spanish club as it weighs up the midfielder's future.

Paz reportedly chose to remain at Como last summer because he wanted to continue developing through regular appearances, and his decision has been rewarded by an outstanding start to the upcoming campaign.

Manchester United have also been linked with the Argentina international, although Madrid's contractual advantage places the Spanish giants in a stronger position.

For Los Blancos, securing a player whose value has risen considerably could represent an attractive investment. For Paz, the sporting challenge would be to turn the promise recognised by Veron into an influential role at a club where competition for attacking positions is already fierce.

Scott has established himself as one of the most sought-after central midfielders in English football having joined Bournemouth from Bristol City back in 2023.

With attentions beginning to turn towards the January transfer window, speculation is mounting that the 23-year-old could have his head turned amid strong interest from the Premier League’s elite.

Though he picked up a thigh injury while on international duty with England last month, Scott’s outstanding performance in the Three Lions’ thumping 7-0 win over Croatia did little to quieten rumours of a potential major-money move.

Arsenal, Manchester City and Tottenham have all been credited with an interest in recent weeks and months, but Chelsea reportedly find themselves in pole position to land Scott this winter.

The Blues are actively scouring the market for midfield reinforcements after failing to bring in a replacement for Enzo Fernandez in the summer and are mentioned to be ‘increasingly confident’ of reaching an agreement for Scott.

Up until this point, Bournemouth have publicly played down speculation that Scott could be on the move, especially midway through the campaign when they risk derailing the side’s encouraging progress under Marco Rose.

However, it’s understood an offer in region of £100million could be enough to convince the Cherries into selling Scott in what would undoubtedly be one of this January’s biggest deals.

One man who knows more than anyone what it takes to thrive in Chelsea’s midfield is Lampard, arguably the club’s greatest ever player, who won 14 trophies across an illustrious 13-year career at Stamford Bridge.

During a wide-ranging interview on the Rio Ferdinand Presents YouTube channel, Lampard made it clear just how highly he rated Scott when he was asked to name his dream Premier League midfield three on current form.

‘I don’t want to leave anyone out because there are some teams that are doing some stuff… I’m loving what Brighton are doing at the moment but you do come back to the bigger players sometimes, maybe Cole Palmer or Rayan Cherki,’ the Coventry head coach told Ferdinand.

‘I love Alex Scott at Bournemouth, I think he’s quality.

‘He’s injured now for a short period but I think he’s real quality in that modern all-rounder [role], in the double six/eight.’.

Revealing other candidates for his midfield three, Lampard added: ‘I’ve got to put Elliot Anderson in there, in my opinion, for the way he’s playing.

‘I’m trying to think of the attacking options… I think I’d put Anderson and Declan Rice as the two sixes and then I’ll go for an eight/ten.

In a recent development, ‘I’m trying to think of the eight-ten that’s really being decisive at the minute. Rayan Cherki is doing bits, I love Cole Palmer.’.

Sources indicate that such is his importance, there is even talk of a renewal being discussed. Musah was interviewed by SportMediaset and it was published two days before the Serie A campaign resumes with a home game against Frosinone. His comments were transcribed by MilanNews.

Do you feel like a ‘wild card’ for Milan?

“A little less so this year because I haven’t changed positions as much, even though I can do that. I’ve been able to play in midfield and improve in that area.”.

It has been revealed that “I think he watched my old games, because he already knew what he expected from me and what he could ask of me. He did his homework, he watched everything, and he already knew what and how he could use me.”.

We’ve never seen you play left-back at Milan like you did in Genoa: how did this idea come about?

“I don’t know (laughs). This question is for the coach. Bartesaghi and Estupinan are very good, but that day he wanted a right-footed player on the left.”.

If it were up to you, where do you want to play most?

It has been revealed that “I think playing in midfield. Not fixed, though, being able to go anywhere so I can get the ball, get deep, without being fixed.”.

Do you think Milan is improving? Is the Scudetto possible?

“It’s possible. We train every day for it. We all have the dream and ambition of winning it, and we’ll do everything we can to get there.”.

Can you tell us what you remember about your time in the States?

What do you remember about America?

In a recent development, “Playing for the United States helped me gain this sense of belonging. Until I was 17, I only had a passport, but now I feel part of the culture.”.

Industry observers note that “I can go there. I know the restaurants, the chains, the people from different states, the geography. I understand American people so much now.

“I have many passports, I lived and grew up in many countries, like here in Italy, in England, so I feel a bit of everything.”.

Have you ever returned to see your childhood homes?

Sources indicate that “Yes, in 2021 I returned to Latest York. I saw the house where I lived that year. The Bronx. It was beautiful to see it. There was a piece missing from my memory, and it was nice to be able to connect it.”.

Is it true you have a cat named Bronx?

Your family moved from America to Italy….

“My family was already in Italy, and my mother had to go back and forth to America.”.

What was your childhood like in Castelfranco Veneto?

Industry observers note that “Beautiful. It’s a place where my parents weren’t afraid to let me play all day outside in the parking lot near the apartment building.”.

Is it true that your parents’ years of financial sacrifice were years of financial hardship?

“Playing for Arsenal was a great privilege, because I arrived from Italy at 9 years old, played with a small team, and immediately joined Arsenal.

“I was ready to move to the first team when I was 16, and Valencia had a initiative for me. I spent four wonderful years in Spain; it’s a city that will always remain in my heart.”.

What’s the atmosphere like in the dressing room?

Is he someone who gets angry when necessary?

“Yes. After Ferencvaros he was very angry, like everyone else.”.

“My wife is from Zanzibar, my family is Ghanaian. So it’s nice to travel to our home countries in the summer.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Premier League clubs have voted to protect the organisation's bigwigs from any individual legal action taken by Manchester City's sponsors.
  • Instead, the clubs - including City themselves - will foot any legal bills incurred by a potential corporate defamation suit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 08:16 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

Premier League clubs have voted to protect the organisation's bigwigs from any individual legal action taken by Manchester City's sponsors.

Instead, the clubs - including City themselves - will foot any legal bills incurred by a potential corporate defamation suit.

Daily Mail Sport understands there was widespread support from clubs to insulate Premier League chief executive Richard Masters and the four other league directors.

The vote passed with 18 clubs in favour, and City and Nottingham Forest against.

It is understood Forest opted to vote that way as they felt they had not been given sufficient information or enough time to consider the proposal and its implications, as opposed to representing a show of support for City.

The matter was the first item on the agenda at the Premier League shareholders' meeting in the Savoy Hotel on Thursday and was addressed swiftly with limited discussion.

Clubs had a paper for the proposed rule change before the meeting and there was significant support to extend the legal protection to individuals on the league's board.

This marks the first time since the Premier League’s inception that insurance arrangements for its board members have been reviewed.

Premier League clubs will foot the bill if Manchester City's sponsors sue for defamation.

In September, City were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules after a seven-year legal process.

An independent commission appointed by the Premier League found City inflated their revenues by £900million – disguising money from their Abu Dhabi ownership group as sponsorship revenue.

Etihad Airways, owned by the Abu Dhabi government, denied being ‘involved in improper commercial arrangements’ and said it was considering legal action in response to the verdict.

Meanwhile, another City sponsor, Etisalat - a telecommunications firm - is also weighing up legal action.

City, though, maintain their innocence and are appealing the decision, which could see them relegated from the top flight.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wes Brown believes Manchester United should still be aiming for a top-five finish this season after Mauricio Pochettino was appointed head coach.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has officially taken the reins at Old Trafford after his final two matches with the United States national team.

Pochettino has undoubtedly been thrown in at the deep end, with United winless in their last eight Premier League matches and facing Liverpool in his first game on Sunday.

But former Red Devils defender Brown believes that the Argentine has the quality to inspire a quick turnaround from his new crop of players.

It has been revealed that ‘Poch is very experienced, and he has his own style of play, but it’s all about consistency, he told Metro. ‘Making the players believe they’re good enough and making sure they do it week in, week out.

‘We’ve had no momentum; we’ve played well here and there in games, and when we did we managed to score, but at the same time we’ve been very poor at times and open to teams scoring at will, making loads of mistakes.

‘The confidence isn’t there, but he’ll be coming in and just trying to get consistency through the team.

‘When a upcoming manager comes in, the players really make an effort, that’s just the way it goes, but then it’s up to the manager to keep that going through the season, and whether or not he’ll be able to, we’ll all have to see.’.

Pochettino brings with him extensive experience in the Premier League but also a proven track record of nurturing young talent into the first team.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

And Brown is hopeful that academy duo Shea Lacey and Harry Amass could benefit from the Argentine’s arrival, adding: ‘If anyone, you think those two might come in and get a game under the new manager to show what they can do.

Industry observers note that ‘I think at the moment, you are looking at Shea Lacey and thinking, “Yeah, he can get a game”. He delivers, he runs, he works hard.

‘But I also think when you’re in a position where you don’t necessarily just bring in the young lads as well. I think that’s a tough gig if I’m being honest, and you can’t just bring them in when the team’s like this.’.

Pochettino will have to endure a frenetic start to life in the United dugout, with a run of eight games in 21 days starting at Anfield on Sunday.

But with plenty of the season still ahead, Brown thinks United should still be aiming high if they can start fast under their eighth permanent boss since Alex Ferguson’s retirement.

‘There’s still a chance of getting into Europe, 100 per cent,’ Brown added, speaking to Metro ahead of the year’s second Counter-Strike Major.

Sources indicate that ‘Even though it’s been very disappointing, even if you look at the table now, the gap is not that big. It’s maybe 8-9 points from a European place, if that.

‘So you’ve still got to have that in the back of your mind. It’s Manchester United; that’s where you aim to be, if not higher, and I’m sure Poch will definitely be looking to get us in that sort of area and going in that direction.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England captain Harry Kane has undergone successful surgery on an ankle ligament injury which is expected to keep him sidelined for three months.

The recently crowned Ballon d’Or winner started for Bayern Munich as they drew with Cologne on Friday evening, but was forced off after just 20 minutes.

It has been revealed that he was caught in a late tackle by Joel Schmied as he looked to latch onto a Michael Olise cross and immediately went down clutching his lower leg. He attempted to play on, but after spending a few minutes as a virtual bystander, he signalled to the bench that he could not continue.

It was confirmed at full-time he had suffered a tear to the syndesmotic ligament in his ankle, with Bayern head coach Vincent Kompany predicting he would miss around three months.

And on Saturday morning the club confirmed he had undergone successful surgery on the injury, with the ball now rolling on a lengthy period of rehabilitation.

Kane later shared a photo of himself on the edge of a hospital bed, bearing a broad grin and brandishing two thumbs-ups despite wearing a protective boot on his left foot.

He wrote: “The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!

“‘Tough times don’t last, tough people do’ - my guy [NFL legend Julian Edelman] told me this one!

“Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut!”.

Ankle injuries plagued Kane throughout his 14-year stint at Tottenham, but he has largely managed to stay fit since moving to Munich in 2023.

Sources indicate that it remains to be seen whether Kane will be fit in time to lead England out in the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2027. The two legs of that tie will be played on March 27 and 30.

The projected three-month rehabilitation period suggests he will be back in contention in late February, and Thomas Tuchel will hope he can get back fit and firing in time to don the captain’s armband in Oslo.

Sources indicate that kane has been fielding plenty of well wishes. England’s official Instagram account replied to his post confirming his succesful surgery, writing in a comment: “Wishing you a speedy recovery, Harry!”.

Chelsea and England forward Morgan Rogers has also joined Joshua Kimmich, Manuel Neuer and Dayot Upamecano in sending their support to the 33-year-old.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Andriy Shevchenko has demanded an apology from Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk after he blamed Ukraine’s national team for his failed drugs test.
  • Mudryk, who is on loan at Tottenham Hotspur from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 to July 2026 after he tested positive for the banned substance meldonium.
  • The 25-year-old initially faced a four-year ban but returned to football this summer after he accepted that he had breached anti-doping rules and agreed to a suspension equal to the time he had already served.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andriy Shevchenko has demanded an apology from Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk after he blamed Ukraine’s national team for his failed drugs test.

Mudryk, who is on loan at Tottenham Hotspur from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 to July 2026 after he tested positive for the banned substance meldonium.

The 25-year-old initially faced a four-year ban but returned to football this summer after he accepted that he had breached anti-doping rules and agreed to a suspension equal to the time he had already served.

Speaking to YouTube channel Guest of Gordon this week, Mudryk was asked who he felt was to blame for the adverse finding.

‘The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team,’ Mudryk stated.

‘It should never have existed. I probably haven’t stated it publicly yet but I’m saying it now.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.’.

Recent findings suggest that asked how meldonium got into his system, Mudryuk said: ‘The Ukrainian national team has absolutely no security system. At clubs, when you travel to an away game, there are always people responsible for what happens on the hotel floors and in the team.

It has been revealed that ‘There are people who keep an eye on it. In the Ukrainian national team we have a nutritionist who hands us pills every couple of days before games. He brings us a little cup. Everyone has to take the pills that are in that cup.’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Former Chelsea striker Shevchenko, who is now the president of the Ukrainian Association of Football, has hit back at Mudryk’s claims and has described the winger’s version of events as ‘baseless slander’.

‘I want to express my position on the accusations of Mykhailo Mudryk. Loud statements were made about the UAF, the Ukrainian national team. This is a baseless slander against our people, who do their job honestly and professionally,’ Shevchenko mentioned in a statement to Tribuna Ukraine.

‘Instead, after the suspension of Mykhailo Mudryk, his representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to artificially find an employee who would take responsibility for the appearance of meldonium in his doping sample.

‘The UAF refused – such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work. The accusations from Mykhailo’s representatives were not confirmed or proven after many studies and inspections. The investigation and the final settlement agreement with WADA and the English association confirm this.

Sources indicate that ‘After Mykhailo became a Chelsea player, the club sent a letter to the UAF requesting that he not be given any medication during the national team training camp. The team staff complied with this request.

According to recent reports, ‘Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also agreed for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him during the training camp. These people monitored his regimen and recovery and helped him with his daily life.

It has been revealed that ‘The UAF has completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk’s representatives with the information they requested and have been in contact with those who worked on the case.

Sources indicate that ‘I know people who have been working in the national team for many years. I trust them, because during all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make one doubt their professionalism.

Industry observers note that ‘If Mykhailo has evidence to support his words, let him provide it. If there is no such evidence, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he questioned.’.

Manchester United are considering a move for Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic in the January transfer window, according to reports.

Mauricio Pochettino arrived at United this week having replaced Michael Carrick, who was sacked during the international break.

But the Argentine begins his tenure at Old Trafford without a recognised striker as Benjamin Sesko is sidelined until next year due to a shin injury.

United have made funds available to strengthen Pochettino’s squad in January and the club are targeting a fresh striker.

According to The i Paper, Matanovic is on United’s striker shortlist alongside Folarin Balogun, who Monaco are open to selling in the January transfer window.

The report adds that United are also looking to bolster Pochettino’s defence with Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey and left-back Antonee Robinson under consideration.

Matanovic, meanwhile, was signed by Freiburg in an €8 million (£6.8m) deal from Eintracht Frankfurt last year.

The Croatia international, who offers a physical presence in attack at 6ft 5in, has scored 23 goals in 64 games for Freiburg so far.

At international level, Matanovic has scored two goals in 17 appearances for Croatia and came off the bench in three games at the World Cup in the summer.

Matanovic, who is now valued at around €30m (£26m), has also been linked with a move to Tottenham.

When asked about his future in September, Matanovic insisted he had not received an approach to leave Freiburg.

‘As for me, I’m presently in Freiburg. There has been absolutely no contact with anyone from my side,’ the striker noted.

Latest transfer news and rumours.

AC Milan are reportedly considering a move for Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes, who has rejected another new contract offer at Old Trafford.

According to Corriere dello Sport, Milan are keeping an eye on Fernandes’ situation at United, with the possibility of a move being explored should circumstances allow.

The midfielder’s contract status could make him an attractive target for the Rossoneri, although no formal negotiations or agreement have been reported at this stage.

The Mexican was the Blues’ set-piece coach, but he has now moved to Selhurst Park to become a more general first-team coach under upcoming boss Thomas Frank.

Mykhailo Mudryk has revealed that he wanted to join Arsenal.

The Tottenham winger, on loan from Chelsea, admitted that before he signed for the Blues in January 2023, he had wanted to move to north London.

Before he made the move to Stamford Bridge, he had been heavily linked with a move to Mikel Arteta’s side, but ultimately, he decided to join Graham Potter’s Blues instead.

Now, he has declared that his real desire was a move to Arsenal, which never materialised.

  • In their previous league outing, Les Olympiens claimed a commendable 2-1 victory over Lens at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis, while Les Manceaux scored late against Monaco on home soil to salvage a point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Freddie Cotton | 20 Nov 2026 21:07, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:15.

Marseille welcome Le Mans to the Stade Velodrome on Sunday evening for round 11 of the 2026-27 Ligue 1 campaign.

In their previous league outing, Les Olympiens claimed a commendable 2-1 victory over Lens at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis, while Les Manceaux scored late against Monaco on home soil to salvage a point.

Following a dismal start to the current league campaign, losing five of their opening six matches to leave them languishing inside the relegation zone and just one point off the foot of the table at the end of September, Marseille will be delighted with how they have bounced back in recent weeks.

Since their narrow 2-1 loss to back-to-back European champions Paris Saint-Germain on September 20, Les Olympiens have been an unstoppable force, winning each of their previous five domestic matches to rise to fourth in the Ligue 1 table and sit just five points off Les Parisiens at the summit.

The biggest strength of Bruno Genesio’s side has undoubtedly been their free flowing attack, as after 10 league games, Marseille have netted an impressive 22 goals, a tally that cannot be bettered by any other side in the division.

However, Les Olympiens will undoubtedly be disappointed with their performances in the UEFA Europa League, as after four league phase fixtures they have picked up just three points and at the moment reside outside of the tournament’s progression places to the knockout stage.

Having gone unbeaten in each of their previous six encounters with Le Mans, including a 2-1 victory in their most recent meeting at the Stade Velodrome in January 2010, Marseille will be confident that they can continue their fine league form this weekend though and mount a charge towards PSG in top spot.

After ending their 16-year wait for promotion to France’s top tier at the end of the 2025-26 campaign, beating Bastia 2-0 away from home on the final day to pip St. Etienne to second place, Le Mans will have mixed feelings about their start to life in Ligue 1 this season.

Although they lost just one of their opening five Ligue 1 matches to start the campaign, Patrick Videira’s men have failed to claim a league victory in over two months, leaving them 15th in the table with eight points and only outside of the relegation places on goal difference.

Without a doubt, Les Manceaux’s weakness in the 2026-27 season has been their leaky defence, as Sunday’s visitors have conceded a concerning 19 league goals so far and are one of three sides alongside Lens and Strasbourg that are yet to keep a clean sheet.

Despite previously claiming victory at the Stade Velodrome, posting a famous 3-2 win in September 1994, Le Mans head into Sunday’s match in poor form, facing Marseille as massive underdogs, and knowing they’ll need to pull off another monumental triumph if they want to get their season back on track this weekend.

Marseille form (all competitions):.

Le Mans form (all competitions):.

Marseille are still without Italian full-back Emerson Palmieri, who is expected to return before the end of the year from a knee problem, while Canadian midfielder Derek Cornelius continues his struggles with a hip problem.

On a more positive note, Genesio will be glad that a cohort of important first team players including the likes of Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Nayef Aguerd and Geoffrey Kondogbia have all returned from the international break unscathed.

Netting an impressive seven Ligue 1 goals so far this season, including one in each of his previous three league outings, Amine Gouiri is undoubtedly Les Olympiens’ dangerman and will be hoping to close the gap to Paris FC’s Lassine Sinayoko at the top of the division’s scoring charts on Sunday evening.

Le Mans are certain to be missing Algerian midfielder Adil Bourabaa and former Everton defender Djibril Sidibe this weekend as the pair are ruled out with ankle and foot injuries respectively.

It remains to be seen whether either Samuel Yohou, who has reportedly sustained a head injury, or young French midfielder Martin Rossignol can fight off problems to feature at the Stade Velodrome too.

After signing from Ligue 2 side Guingamp in the summer, 32-year-old striker Louis Mafouta has been the visitors’ biggest attacking threat this season, scoring a respectable four goals in 10 league matches.

Marseille possible starting lineup:.

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Hojbjerg, Nnadi; Harit, Abdelli, Paixao; Gouiri.

Le Mans possible starting lineup:.

Kocik; Bamba, Torrente, Voyer; Vercruysse; Buades, Traore, Bretelle, Calodat; Mafouta, Gueye.

Having emphatically bounced back from their early season woes, Marseille will be confident that they can beat any opponent they come up against and continue their impressive rise up the table.

Although Le Mans will be desperate to turn around their poor form, we believe the hosts will be far too strong and are backing them to close the gap on the teams above by posting a convincing victory at the Stade Velodrome on Sunday evening.

Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 56 min read (11171 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~56 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • erectus finds in East and Southeast Asia represent a key part of the hominin evolutionary history of the Asian region, with China sitting in an key location to understand the dispersal, interactions and adaptations of this species6,7,8.
  • Establishing the environmental context of H.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Homo erectus represents one of the longest-persisting hominin species, with a geographic range from Africa to eastern Eurasia from approximately 1.9 million years ago1 to 108 thousand years ago (ka)2. Despite this, there are still large gaps in our understanding of the adaptation capabilities of this species and the extent of its persistence in China. Assumptions over ecological preferences based on the Trinil3, Sangiran4 and Ngandong2 (in Java) open woodland–grassland mosaics have persisted, combined with limited direct stable carbon isotope measurements in Asia. Here we present a rich temporal and environmental context for nine hominin teeth, eight of which were morphologically and genetically identified as H. erectus5, found in two sister caves in Guangxi province, southern China. We modelled 43 radiometric ages from five dating techniques to establish a timeline for H. erectus presence in this region. Stable and clumped isotopes and trace elements from teeth were used to establish the dominant environments and their behavioural responses. We show that H. erectus was present in southern China between 324 and 184 ka, which is substantially more recent than previously established in this region for unequivocally H. erectus fossils at approximately 400 ka. The evidence suggests that they were persisting in closed rainforest ecosystems, thought to be the domain of only Homo sapiens, and were demonstrating long-term mobility and ecological flexibility. This evidence challenges the assumptions over the ecological preferences and behavioural limitations of H. erectus.

Early and late H. erectus finds in East and Southeast Asia represent a key part of the hominin evolutionary history of the Asian region, with China sitting in an key location to understand the dispersal, interactions and adaptations of this species6,7,8. There is a rich fossil record for H. erectus in China in Yuanmou (1.7 million years ago)9,10,11, Gongwangling (1.6 million years ago)12, Zhoukoudian (780–400 ka)13, Nanjing (approximately 650 ka)14 and Hexian (410 ka)15 (Supplementary Information 1). However, most of these sites are located in north and central China, with reliably identified and dated H. erectus fossils being conspicuously rare in southern China, especially during the Middle Pleistocene. This makes it particularly challenging to establish their ecological preferences. Furthermore, evidence of younger H. erectus (less than 400 ka) is almost entirely absent from China. This temporal gap is particularly striking given that H. erectus persisted in Java until 117–108 ka at Ngandong2, raising fundamental questions about the species’ distribution, ecological adaptations and ultimate fate in mainland China.

Establishing the environmental context of H. erectus is essential for understanding the species’ ecological flexibility and adaptive capabilities. The youngest Javanese H. erectus at Ngandong2 persisted in woodland refugia as rainforests expanded across the region, raising questions about whether encroaching closed-canopy forests contributed to the species’ eventual extinction2,16. Yet, there have been very few stable isotope studies on H. erectus evidence, as the material is often limited by diagenetic alteration3. Recent work has debated whether non-H. sapiens Middle Pleistocene hominins possessed the adaptive capabilities to exploit tropical rainforest environments17,18. Studying the forested landscapes of tropical southern China during the Middle and Late Pleistocene19 thus provides a crucial test case for assessing H. erectus ecological adaptations. Furthermore, understanding mobility patterns through techniques such as strontium isotope analysis can reveal how these populations used their landscapes and how they connected with contemporaneous populations across broader regional scales20,21.

Since the Pleistocene, tropical forest and grassland environments in southern China have provided a critical biogeographical corridor for faunal dispersals between northern latitudes and insular Southeast Asia22,23,24. The karst landscapes and cave systems of the region have yielded abundant Pleistocene faunal assemblages, yet there is right now no clear evidence that H. erectus was part of the Stegodon–Ailuropoda fauna in this region6. This raises questions as to whether the absence of H. erectus in southern China, particularly during the late Middle Pleistocene, is a consequence of ecological constraints preventing H. erectus from exploiting southern China’s tropical forest environments18, representing an effective biogeographic barrier25, or results from other factors such as an imbalance in research intensity7, a reflection of real absence of the species in the region due to alternative dispersal routes through the Tibetan corridor6, the absence of secure dating data on many out-of-context teeth, the misidentification of fragmentary remains (particularly with morphologically similar Pongo teeth26), taphonomic and preservation biases in tropical environments18, lower population densities leading to reduced fossil representation27 or the occupation of an ecological niche that is not readily preserved in cave deposits18. Distinguishing between these scenarios requires well-dated, robustly identified hominin fossils with detailed environmental context—evidence that has been lacking.

Sources indicate that to provide a temporal and environmental context for the eight H. erectus teeth6 from Baxian and Naxian caves in southern China (Fig. 1, Supplementary Information 2 and 3 and Extended Data Figs. 1–3), we used five independent dating techniques to constrain the sediments: post-infrared infrared-stimulated luminescence (pIR-IRSL) dating of feldspars, optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating of quartz (Supplementary Information 4), uranium-series (U-series) dating of fossil teeth (Supplementary Information 5), coupled U-series–electron spin resonance (US-ESR) dating of fossil teeth (Supplementary Information 6) and U-series dating of carbonate capping flowstones (Supplementary Information 7), all integrated through the use of two Bayesian age models—ChronoModel and OxCal (Supplementary Information 8). Environmental reconstruction was achieved through faunal analysis (Supplementary Information 3), bulk and sequential stable isotope analysis of faunal and H. erectus tooth enamel (Supplementary Information 9) and clumped isotope thermometry of cave sediments (Supplementary Information 10). Finally, we assessed individual mobility patterns through laser-ablation trace element mapping and strontium isotope analysis of hominin tooth enamel, integrated with a regional strontium isoscape constructed using random forest machine learning to identify potential source regions (Supplementary Information 11). These multiple lines of evidence, replicated across laboratories in China and Australia, provide, to our knowledge, the first comprehensive temporal, environmental and behavioural context for late H. erectus in southern China.

It has been revealed that the Naxian and Baxian caves, located 15 km apart and situated 13 km to the northwest and 20 km to the north of Chongzuo City, respectively, are connected by a straight karst valley corridor (Fig. 1, Extended Data Fig. 1a,b,e,f and Supplementary Information 2). They are both horizontal caves at 226 and 218 m above sea level, positioned 5–7 m above the valley floor (Extended Data Fig. 2), with small fossil chambers at the rear of each cave (Fig. 2). The chambers contain remarkably similar dense, cemented, cataclastic breccias that have yielded a combined total of over 18,000 mammalian fossils, which were initially accumulated by porcupines28, including hominin remains (Supplementary Information 2). The fossil-bearing breccias (Extended Data Fig. 3) were capped by thick flowstone and underlain by younger mixed sediments (Extended Data Fig. 1d,h). This similarity suggests deposition under comparable environmental conditions.

In a recent development, of the resulting 45 radiometric ages from both caves (Extended Data Figs. 4–7), 43 were modelled and given similar modelled age estimates (OxCal: 312–161 ka; ChronoModel: 324–184 ka at 2σ uncertainties; Extended Data Fig. 8), but the ChronoModel results were used owing to their greater outlier robustness and more reliable lower age limit. These results indicate that the age of H. erectus fossil evidence lies between 324 and 184 ka for the Baxian caves, and between 319 and 241 ka for the Naxian caves. These error limits are overlapping and broadly contemporaneous, and indicate a 95% probability that H. erectus was in this area sometime between 324 and 184 ka (see Supplementary Information 4–8 for all dating tables, data and discussion of limitations, uncertainties and choice of model; Fig. 3). The overlapping age uncertainties for the caves of approximately 78,000 years suggest a contemporaneous or near-contemporaneous presence on this landscape. The modelled ages are consistent across all five dating techniques within their respective uncertainties, providing robust constraints on the timing of H. erectus presence in this region.
