In a recent development, the faunal assemblages from the Baxian and Naxian caves are taxonomically diverse and remarkably similar in composition (Supplementary Information 3 and Extended Data Fig. 3). Both assemblages include numerous taxa that have since become locally extinct, including Pongo, Elephas and rhinoceros Dicerorhinus, though most remain extant elsewhere in Asia. Notably, H. erectus, Stegodon and ‘Megalovis’ are globally extinct. Habitat preference analysis indicates that both assemblages are strongly dominated by forest-dwelling taxa (Supplementary Fig. 3), which is consistent with predominantly forested landscapes during the time of deposition.

In a recent development, the plant-equivalent stable carbon isotope values for the Baxian faunal teeth, after correction for species-specific diet-to-enamel enrichment factors based on body mass29 (Supplementary Information 9), range from −31.5 to −23.0‰ (average = −27.6 ± 1.87‰ (1σ)), while lower values observed at the Naxian cave range from −34.0 to −25.1‰ (average = −29.4 ± 2.45‰ (1σ)). Both assemblages yield values well below the dense-canopy forest threshold of −27.5‰ (ref. 28), with no evidence of C4 plant consumption or even C3–C4 intermediate signatures (Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 9). These data indicate that the fauna at both sites derived their dietary carbon exclusively from C3 vegetation, with the frequency of canopy-related values exceeding those reported for equatorial African rainforest systems29 and being comparable to that documented for western Amazonian forests30,31,32. This pattern is particularly notable given that several of the taxa represented in the assemblages are known elsewhere to exploit mixed C3–C4 resources or to incorporate substantial C4-derived inputs into their diets in more open environments16.

It has been revealed that independent oxygen isotope (δ18O) and clumped isotope (Δ47) analyses further support these environmental reconstructions, indicating humid tropical conditions with higher precipitation and cooler temperatures than modern values in this region (Extended Data Fig. 9 and Supplementary Information 9 and 10).

It has been revealed that three H. erectus teeth from the Naxian cave (NX-B1, NX-B2 and NX-A1) show similarly low isotopic values, with carbon values ranging from −15.0 to −14.0‰, which fall at the boundary between dense-canopy forest and more open C3 vegetation. Although the dataset is limited (n = 3) and presently restricted to the Naxian locality, these values are fully consistent with those observed across the much larger faunal assemblage and fall within the range expected for consumers deriving their dietary carbon from closed-canopy C3 vegetation, demonstrating that these late H. erectus populations exploited tropical rainforest resources.

High-resolution trace element mapping on one H. erectus individual from the Baxian cave (PA1799) yielded 87Sr/86Sr ratios ranging from 0.7110 to 0.7220 (Supplementary Information 11 and Extended Data Fig. 10), while three H. erectus teeth sampled from the Naxian cave demonstrated overlapping but distinct ranges. All four individuals indicate either movement between geologically distinct regions or consumption of resources from multiple locations during childhood (2–6 years), corresponding to the period of tooth formation.

Recent findings suggest that A regional strontium isoscape for southern China and northern Southeast Asia33 (Supplementary Information 11) reveals substantial spatial heterogeneity in predicted 87Sr/86Sr ratios, with the local Baxian–Naxian region characterized by relatively homogeneous values (0.710–0.715), reflecting the dominant Carboniferous–Permian limestone karst geology (Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 10). More radiogenic signatures (0.717–0.723) occur to the west and northwest in mountainous areas underlain by Precambrian and Palaeozoic metamorphic rocks, while intermediate to more radiogenic values (0.715–0.720) characterize regions to the south, including the Red River valley of northern Vietnam.

In a recent development, geographic assignment probability maps generated for three representative 87Sr/86Sr values observed in the human tooth profiles indicate that these H. erectus individuals may have moved between the local limestone karst regions and more distant areas during childhood, with the most radiogenic signatures potentially pointing towards areas as far afield as northern Vietnam, which connect southern China with mainland Southeast Asia (Figs. 1 and 3 and Extended Data Fig. 10).

Our results demonstrate that H. erectus was present in southern China between 324 and 184 ka (Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 8), representing, to our knowledge, the youngest reliably dated occurrence of this species in China and the first with robust chronological constraints from southern China. The integration of multiple independent dating techniques combined with Bayesian age modelling provides unprecedented temporal resolution for late H. erectus in mainland Asia. These findings fundamentally alter our understanding of the species’ persistence and distribution in China, extending the documented record by more than 200,000 years beyond the previous youngest occurrences in Hexian and Nanjing14,15, and establishing southern China as a key region for late-surviving populations during the late Middle Pleistocene (for example, ref. 19).

The temporal importance of this discovery extends beyond simply filling a chronological gap. The age uncertainty range of 324–184 ka places these H. erectus populations at some point within marine isotope stages 9 through 6, raising intriguing questions about potential contemporaneity or overlap with Homo longi (Denisovans) identified in Cobra cave (Laos)34, Baishiya cave (Tibetan Plateau)35, Harbin (northeast China)36,37,38 and the Penghu Channel off the western shore of Taiwan39. The temporal proximity of these various hominin populations across China during the late Middle Pleistocene suggests a more complex biogeographical landscape than previously recognized, with multiple hominin lineages potentially coexisting across different ecological zones and elevational gradients.

It has been revealed that moreover, the environmental context revealed by our multi-proxy analyses challenges prevailing assumptions about late H. erectus ecological constraints and mobility patterns. The combined evidence demonstrates unequivocally that these late H. erectus populations exploited closed-canopy tropical rainforest environments and may have conducted long-distance movement beyond the local karst terrain during childhood. The ecological implications of this rainforest use and mobility are profound. Archaeological evidence has so far suggested that H. sapiens was the only member of our genus to specialize in the regular exploitation of these environments18, as early as 150 ka in western Africa40,41. In Southeast Asia, recent isotopic observations of declines in C4 environments and expansion of rainforest in the Middle to early Late Pleistocene have been associated with the disappearance of non-H. sapiens hominin taxa42,43, seemingly unable to shift from mixed savannah–woodland habitats to these increasingly closed forests16,44. However, our data directly challenge this view by demonstrating that H. erectus was not ecologically excluded from rainforest environments (Fig. 3) and that long-distance mobility into these environments may have been a common behavioural pattern rather than exceptional behaviour by isolated individuals.

These findings contrast markedly with Early and Middle Pleistocene H. erectus occupations at Trinil3 and Sangiran in Java4 (Extended Data Fig. 9b). The youngest Javanese H. erectus at Ngandong2 persisted in relatively open woodland refugia2, leading to suggestions that expanding rainforests may have contributed to the species’ eventual extinction in Java2,16. Among early hominin-bearing sites in East and Southeast Asia (Extended Data Fig. 9b), the Naxian and Baxian cave results most closely resemble those from Lida Ajer, Sumatra (73–63 ka), an early H. sapiens site also characterized by closed-canopy rainforest45. This demonstrates that H. erectus was, at minimum, capable of persisting among rainforest fauna, even if such habitats did not represent its optimal ecological niche.

Areas in northern Vietnam, such as the Red River valley (Figs. 1 and 3), have long been recognized as a critical biogeographical corridor connecting the karst uplands of southern China with the lowlands of mainland Southeast Asia24. The limited strontium isotope evidence tentatively suggests that late H. erectus populations may have been utilizing similar corridors for seasonal movements, long-distance migrations or resource procurement. This large range (potentially around 250 km) through mostly enclosed environments challenges assumptions about the limited ranging behaviour of H. erectus and suggests behavioural sophistication in landscape use.

Sources indicate that our findings collectively demonstrate that late Middle Pleistocene H. erectus was present in southern China, surviving contemporaneously with H. longi and exhibiting considerable ecological and behavioural flexibility. Rather than being restricted to open savanna or woodland habitats, as traditionally assumed, these populations persisted in closed-canopy tropical rainforests while simultaneously engaging in potential long-distance mobility across diverse ecological and geological landscapes. This evidence challenges the characterization of H. erectus as a species unable to exploit complex tropical forest environments. Whether these adaptations were specific to the late-surviving populations in southern China alone remains to be seen, but further stable isotope work on other Middle Pleistocene sites is vital to address this question. However, the presence of morphologically and genetically confirmed H. erectus in southern China between 324 and 184 ka, combined with the environmental and suggested mobility evidence, is sufficient to necessitate a re-evaluation of the species’ adaptive capabilities, biogeographical range and ultimate fate in mainland Asia.

Recent findings suggest that the caves were discovered using local knowledge and targeted reconnaissance hunting for breccia in the rear chambers. The locations of test pits within the caves were selected on the basis of these reconnaissance surveys. Excavation grids were based on the shape of cave passages and distribution of fossil-rich deposits. Jackhammers were used to break blocks of fossil breccia, and the fossils were extracted using geological hammers. Fine cleaning, identification and cataloguing were conducted in the laboratories at Shandong University and the Institute of Vertebrate Palaeontology and Palaeoanthropology (IVPP).

The fossil-bearing breccia and associated sediments from the fossil chambers of both caves were sampled in situ under subdued red-light conditions (Fig. 2a,d) and were processed using standard sample purification procedures for quartz and feldspar separation including a 40% and 10% wash in hydrofluoric acid for 45 and 10 mins, respectively46. Single aliquots of 90–125 µm feldspar and 180–212 µm quartz or feldspar grains were processed in a Riso TL-DA-20 equipped with an automated DASH set-up, a dual-laser single-grain attachment47 and a blue- and ultraviolet-sensitive Electron Tube photo-multiplier tube (PDM9107Q-AP-TTL-03), using either a blue filter pack (Schott BG-39, 2 mm, and Corning 7-59, 4 mm) for feldspars or U340 filters (2 × Hoya U340, 3.5 mm) for quartz. Data were collected using Sequence Pro v.4.65 and analysed in Analyst v.4.57, DRAC v.1.3 and on spreadsheets designed in Microsoft Excel 365 v.2607. Feldspar equivalent doses were corrected according to the results of the anomalous fading tests (using a weighted mean fading rate of 2.0 ± 0.2% per decade)48, but no residual corrections were undertaken, and the equivalent doses for both feldspar and quartz were then run through either a central age model for the single-aliquot results or a minimum age model49 to identify the single-grain population that experienced the most bleaching before burial. All luminescence analysis was conducted at the ‘Traps’ luminescence dating facility at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia.

Measurements of 238U, 235U, 232Th and 40K were estimated using Geiger–Muller multi-counter beta counting and thick-source alpha counting of dried and powdered sediment samples in the laboratory, combined with in situ gamma spectrometry in the field. The corresponding (dry) beta and gamma dose rates were obtained using the conversion factors in ref. 50 and the beta-dose attenuation factors in ref. 51. Cosmic-ray dose rates were estimated from previously published relationships52, making allowance for the sediment overburden at the sample locality (ranging from 3.99 to 0.20 m), the altitude (ranging from 2,000 to 176 m above sea level) and geomagnetic latitude and longitude of the sampling sites.

According to recent reports, seven H. erectus teeth from the Naxian (n = 6) and Baxian (n = 1) caves were analysed for U-series dating across two laboratories in China and Australia. U-series measurements were undertaken using a laser-ablation multi-collector inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer (MC-ICP-MS) at the Geoarchaeology and Archaeometry Research Group (GARG), Southern Cross University, according to protocols in ref. 53 and in a Neptune MC-ICP-MS at the School of Geography Science, Nanjing Normal University according to refs. 54,55. Laser ablation (at Southern Cross University) was performed with a New Wave Research 213 nm laser, and thorium (230Th, 232Th) and uranium (234U, 235U, 238U) isotopes were measured on a Thermo Neptune XT MC-ICP-MS. Teeth were ablated using rasters of 5 min each and were measured with standards before and after. Uranium and thorium were separated using conventional anion-exchange chromatography at Nanjing, and the U–Th solution was then introduced into the MC-ICP-MS via a DSN-100 desolvation nebulizer system. Isotopic ratios were measured using a detector configuration that allows for the simultaneous measurement of U and Th isotopes56,57.

In a recent development, one H. erectus tooth and one Pongo tooth from the Baxian cave (n = 2) were selected for coupled ESR and U-series dating at GARG, Southern Cross University. Enamel fragments from each tooth were separated using a hand-held diamond saw following the protocol developed in ref. 58. Fragments were then measured at room temperature on a Freiberg MS5000 ESR X-band spectrometer at a modulation amplitude of 0.1 mT, 10 scans, 2 mW power, 100 G sweep and 100 kHz modulation frequency. Each fragment was irradiated, following exponentially increasing irradiation times. Sediment elemental concentrations, external beta and gamma dose rate contributions, and water content were obtained from in situ measurements. The external beta-dose rates have been extrapolated from the U, Th and K contents measured on a portion of sediment sub-sample (approximately 8 g). The external gamma dose rates were determined in situ using a portable gamma spectrometer at each site. The equivalent doses were estimated using Matlab-based MCdose software v.2.0.

Separate sub-samples were hand-drilled from the fresh cross-section of the in situ capping flowstones from Naxian and Baxian caves and processed at the Radiogenic Isotope Facility, University of Queensland (n = 6), and six soda straws and one sample of secondary calcite cement were processed at the School of Geography Science, Nanjing Normal University (n = 7). The powdered sub-samples were subjected to chemical treatment and isotopic measurements by mass spectrometry56. U-series dating of the speleothem samples were conducted at the University of Queensland using a Nu Plasma MC-ICP-MS, and analytical procedures followed previous publications for MC-ICP-MS57,58,59. The 230Th/234U ages were calculated using Isoplot EX 3.75 (ref. 60) and half-lives of 75,690 years for 230Th and 245,250 years for 234U (ref. 61). U-series dating of the speleothem samples was carried out at Nanjing Normal University using a Neptune MC-ICP-MS. U-series ages were calculated using the half-lives of 75,584 years for 230Th and 245,620 years for 234U (ref. 62). Non-radiogenic 230Th was corrected using an assumed bulk-Earth atomic 230Th/232Th ratio of (4.4 ± 2.2) × 10−6 (refs. 54,55).

According to recent reports, two Bayesian modelling programs were used to analyse selected independent age estimates (n = 43) (Supplementary Information 8) and to evaluate the uncertainties associated with the combined dating techniques applied to both sites (Supplementary Tables 7–15): OxCal (v.4.4.4, available at https://c14.arch.ox.ac.uk/oxcal.html)63 and ChronoModel (v.3.2.7, https://chronomodel.com/)64. The analyses incorporated the probability distributions of individual ages, constraints imposed by stratigraphic relationships and the reported minimum or maximum nature of some of the individual age estimates. Each individual age was included as a Gaussian distribution (with mean and s.d. defined by the age estimate and their associated uncertainties), and the resulting age ranges for each phase of deposition were presented at 2σ. OxCal allows the identification of boundary ages between each layer to constrain the fossil layer and ChronoModel was applied to assess the extent to which identical or similar data could be obtained. Both modelling results have been presented for transparency.

Three H. erectus specimens from the Naxian cave, as well as 47 faunal teeth from the Baxian cave and 38 from the Naxian cave (n = 41 in total), were taxonomically identified and prepared for stable isotope analysis, following established preparation methods65 (but see refs. 66,67). The resulting δ13C and δ18O values were measured using a ThermoFisher MAT253+ in six separate measurement blocks per sample at the Earth and Environmental Sciences’ Stable Isotope Geochemistry Laboratory at the University of Queensland. The evolved CO2 gases from the Naxian teeth were analysed for carbon and oxygen isotope compositions using a Thermo Delta V Advantage isotope ratio mass spectrometer housed at the Key Laboratory of Archaeological Sciences and Technology, Shandong University. Stable isotope measurements on the three H. erectus teeth were carried out at the Service de spectrométrie de masse isotopique du Muséum national d’Histoire naturelle, Paris, and analysed using a Thermo Delta V Advantage isotope ratio mass spectrometer. To assess isotopic differences among sites, we applied non-parametric and multivariate tests. For univariate comparisons, Kruskal–Wallis tests revealed highly significant differences in both δ13Ccarbon source (χ² = 181.5, d.f. = 6, P < 0.001) and δ18O (χ² = 114.4, d.f. = 6, P < 0.001) among sites. All statistical analyses were conducted using the open-source program R software (v.4.5.1)68.

Three in situ samples were collected in bulk (CBAX2, CBAX3, CBAX4) from the breccia at Baxian and the clumped isotope analysis was undertaken in the Macquarie GeoAnalytical Stable Isotope Facility using a ThermoFisher dual-inlet MAT253+ mass spectrometer. The results were processed using the Easotope software package69. The final Δ47 value for each sample was then averaged and reported with 95% confidence intervals, before temperatures were calculated using the calibration in ref. 70 for 90 °C reactions. Using these temperatures, the oxygen isotopic composition of the precipitating fluid (δ18Ofluid) was calculated using the equation in ref. 71.

According to recent reports, one H. erectus tooth from Baxian was sectioned with a high-precision diamond saw and polished to a smoothness of greater than 5 μm. Laser ablation combined with ICP-MS was used for trace elemental mapping analyses using an ESI NWR193 coupled to an Agilent 7900 ICP-MS at GARG, Southern Cross University, according to the procedures in refs. 19,72. A laser spot size of 40 μm, a scan speed of 80 μm s−¹, a laser intensity of 60% (approximately 1 J mm−2) and a total integration time of 0.50 s were used to produce data points that corresponded to a pixel size of approximately 40 × 40 μm. NIST610 and NIST612 (certified standard reference materials) were used to assess signal drift. Strontium isotope analysis (87Sr/86Sr) was conducted on four H. erectus teeth: one from Baxian cave and three from Naxian cave, also using laser-ablation MC-ICP-MS at the GARG facility. Enamel fragments were carefully extracted from regions showing low uranium concentrations and distinct elemental signatures from the surrounding dentine according to the mapping results. To contextualize the 87Sr/86Sr values obtained and assess potential mobility patterns, a regional strontium isoscape was constructed for southern China and northern Southeast Asia. The isoscape modelling was based on random forest ensemble machine learning analyses adapted from the original script developed in ref. 33 and followed the method fully described in ref. 21.

K.E.W., Y.Z., R.J.-B., W.L., W.W., C.J., Y.W., W.Y., Y.P. and L.Y. explored and excavated the sites and collected faunal and dating samples, K.E.W. conducted the luminescence dating, R.J.-B., W.Y. and Q.S. conducted the U-series and coupled U-series–ESR dating of the teeth, and J.-x.Z. and Q.S. conducted the U-series measurements on the speleothem. R.J.-B. conducted the trace element analysis and V.B. conducted the isoscape work. M.Q., S.M., L.H. and A.-M.B. conducted stable isotope analysis on the fossil teeth, and N.B. and P.R. conducted isotope data analysis. M.Q. and S.M. conducted the clumped isotope analysis of the breccia, Y.Z., Y.P. and A.-M.B. analysed the fauna and K.E.W. designed the dating approach and conducted the Bayesian modelling. R.K., C.Z., W.L., R.D.Á., F.W., Z.W. and Q.F. worked on the hominin teeth. Finally, K.E.W., R.J.-B., W.L. and Y.Z. wrote the paper, with contributions from all co-authors.

According to recent reports, a-d Naxian cave, a and b the cave – location marked with a red star - is situated on the outer cone of a karst inselberg located close to a highway. c a montage of images to demonstrate the speleology of the cave with the small entrance and flowstone step that leads into the stalagmite chamber dense with speleothem, a larger chamber with narrow and high ceilings and terminating with a small fossil chamber with breccia, d the fossil bearing breccia at the highest point of the cave capped with flowstone and underlain by a younger underlying mixed material below. e-h Baxian Cave e and f the cave is also situated on the outer edge of a karst cone with the limestone corridor than connects both caves, cave location is marked with a red star, g a montage of images to demonstrate the speleology and sedimentology of the cave from the wide and high entrance to the narrower and smaller passage that lead to the confined fossil chamber, h the fossil bearing breccia at the highest point of the cave capped with flowstone and underlain with the younger underlying mixed material. There is a remarkable similarity between the stratigraphy and sedimentology of these deposits and associated fossils (d, h).

In a recent development, a Naxian profile, b Baxian profile illustrating the changing speleology and cave deposits from the upper fossil chambers down to the entrances. Baxian is longer than Naxian but slopes at a lesser angle than the steeper Naxian. Images illustrate the main features found in both caves including a wider chamber and smaller fossil chambers. The images of the fossil chambers are taken from a 3D models of the caves (Supplementary Information 2 for links).

Latest Update: The Premier League’s newest managers have a lot to lose

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In Mauricio Pochettino and Thomas Frank respectively, Manchester United and Crystal Palace have gone for a pair of managers whose reputations in English football could do with a good start this weekend to avoid the varying levels of doom that have surrounded Old Trafford and Selhurst Park from peaking again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Farewell then, Michael Carrick and Pierre Sage, who have gone off to the great big Premier League managerial scrapheap in the sky after an international break where only the identity of the next James Bond could rival speculation over Carrick’s eventual replacement in particular.

In Mauricio Pochettino and Thomas Frank respectively, Manchester United and Crystal Palace have gone for a pair of managers whose reputations in English football could do with a good start this weekend to avoid the varying levels of doom that have surrounded Old Trafford and Selhurst Park from peaking again.

It’s a good thing, then, that despite their contrasting styles, both are known for putting emphasis on energy – not just in how their team plays on the pitch, but in how the culture around the club feels off it.

Pochettino has made headlines before for his love of lemons (they absorb negative energy, he’ll have you know) and his apparent sixth sense. In his 2017 book Brave New World, he wrote: ‘What most influences my decisions is my ability to see if the right energy is flowing.’.

What kind of energy he felt flowing through director of football Jason Wilcox is anyone’s guess at this stage, but his emphasis on things like togetherness and the mindset of his players could finally be the key to starting to turn the Suez canal tanker that United have become, on the pitch at least.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

If Pochettino comes across as part high-level manager, part yoga teacher, then Frank has the air of an executive ready to rebuild the culture at an ailing business.

Sources indicate that A year off from football was on the cards after he was sacked by Tottenham in February. The Dane turned down Palace during the summer in favour of World Cup punditry and attending the Tour de France, and didn’t sound completely convinced he’d made the right decision to cut that break short.

In a recent development, ‘I was a little bit, “When do I want to go back in? Is it now?” Then this opportunity came up,’ he told PalaceTV this week. ‘I was thinking, this is probably too good to turn down. When I’m sitting here, walking around the training ground, it was just, “Okay, you’re back”, which scared me a little bit, but it’s good.’ Consider the troops rallied.

Sources indicate that questions surround the suitability of both appointments, as Pochettino’s biggest success at Spurs was built on the back of a young, mobile team with something to prove and Frank’s at Brentford came as part of a well-oiled machine. You’d be waiting a long time for anyone to describe United or Palace as either of those these days.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Sources indicate that there’s hope to be found too, for those willing to look for it. Frank did only really have half a bad season and the perceived wisdom is that his personality will suit a ‘smaller’ club – as long as he stays away from any Brighton-branded coffee cups – while of all the managers tasked with fixing United, Pochettino does have the air of a man who can become a messianic figure.

Managerial reputations can only survive a certain number of kicks before there’s no coming back and there may not be many chances left for either man at this level if things go pear-shaped.

However, with both teams playing pretty much every three days for the next month, there are plenty of opportunities for their new managers to shift the vibes back towards a positive setting.

And even if the wins don’t start flowing, transfer enthusiasts should have something to cling on to as Palace and United are reportedly ready to back their new men with some signings once the January window opens.

It’s nice to have something to look forward to after Christmas, at least.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 21:13.
  • Roberto D'Aversa's Sassuolo tenure begins against Genoa on Sunday, with the Neroverdi in danger of slipping into the relegation zone.
  • The matchday 12 encounter pits two sides separated by four places in the Serie A table, with the higher-ranked Rossoblu chasing a fifth consecutive victory in this fixture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 21:13.

Roberto D'Aversa's Sassuolo tenure begins against Genoa on Sunday, with the Neroverdi in danger of slipping into the relegation zone.

The matchday 12 encounter pits two sides separated by four places in the Serie A table, with the higher-ranked Rossoblu chasing a fifth consecutive victory in this fixture.

Sassuolo's brief association with Alberto Aquilani lasted just 11 league matches, with the board in Reggio Emilia making another managerial change to arrest the club's poor run of results.

Admittedly, the Black and Greens made a respectable start under the former midfielder, collecting seven points from their opening four games as a three-match unbeaten run followed an opening-day 2-1 defeat at Atalanta BC.

However, mid-September's 2-1 reverse at Monza began a seven-match winless league sequence, and Sassuolo's defensive record under Aquilani made for grim reading.

The Neroverdi conceded a staggering 19 goals across five defeats, losing 4-2 to Frosinone, 2-0 to Como, 6-2 to Lazio, 4-2 to Fiorentina and 3-0 at Roma.

The defeat at the Olimpico proved the final straw for the 17th-placed outfit, who sit just one point clear of the relegation zone and two ahead of 19th-placed Venezia.

That underlines the scale of the task facing D'Aversa, who inherits a side that have conceded 29 Serie A goals, four more than both Monza and bottom-placed Udinese, two of the teams currently occupying the relegation places.

Daniele De Rossi's men will hope that the latest boss needs time to adapt to his surroundings as they seek to extend the Black and Greens' losing sequence.

The travelling supporters will welcome this weekend's trip, given that the Grifone have claimed four consecutive victories in this fixture, including two at Mapei Stadium.

Beyond those recent successes in Reggio Emilia, the Ligurian outfit enter this weekend as one of the competition's form teams.

Their 2-1 home defeat to AC Milan before the international break ended Genoa's three-match winning streak, during which they stunned Juventus 2-0 in front of their supporters.

Having collected 12 points from their last 18 in Serie A, losing to Roma and Milan during that improved run, De Rossi's men will back themselves to overcome any new-manager bounce in Emilia-Romagna and claim consecutive away league victories for the first time since November-December 2024, when they beat Parma 1-0 and Udinese 2-0.

D'Aversa has several fitness concerns ahead of his first Sassuolo match: Cristian Volpato, Yeferson Paz, Daniel Boloca, Domenico Berardi and Vasilije Adzic will be assessed before Sunday's clash; however, Fedde Leysen (knee) and Ismael Kone (broken leg) are sidelined.

If three-goal Adzic cannot feature, the new manager will have to rely on Sebastiano Esposito and Armand Lauriente, who have scored twice apiece, to shoulder more of the Black and Greens' attacking burden.

Genoa, meanwhile, will look to Milutin Osmajic and Junior Messias to add to their respective Serie A tallies of four and two goals, while Stephan El Shaarawy has registered two assists in his last three appearances for the Ligurian outfit.

A relatively healthy squad further boosts the visitors' prospects, although Morten Frendrup remains doubtful due to the ankle problem that kept him out of the Rossoblu's defeat to Milan last time out.

Sassuolo possible starting lineup:.

Muric; Walukiewicz, Caleta-Car, Idzes, Doig; Thorstvedt, Matic, Sulemana; Dominguez, Lauriente; Esposito.

Genoa possible starting lineup:.

Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ehizibue, Wiafe, Traore, Ellertsson; Junior Messias, El Shaarawy; Osmajic.

Sassuolo's injury doubts complicate D'Aversa's first assignment, particularly with Berardi and Adzic potentially unavailable to bolster an attack already struggling to compensate for the team's defensive frailties.

Genoa arrive with fewer fitness concerns and a confident Osmajic, suggesting that De Rossi's men can secure a fifth successive victory over the Neroverdi.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau.

Industry observers note that I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Tottenham will pay tribute to renowned journalist and broadcaster Danny Kelly during their Premier League clash with Ipswich after he passed away last week at the age of 69.

Kelly, a lifelong Spurs fan who edited the NME and Q magazine, and released the Football 365 website before going on to be a presenter and pundit on the BBC and TalkSport, passed away following a battle with oesophageal cancer.

Spurs paid tribute to Kelly in an emotional statement last week and will follow that up by honouring him at today’s game at home to Ipswich.

“The entire Tottenham family mourns the loss of one of our own, broadcasting legend Danny Kelly,” the statement read.

In a recent development, “Our thoughts and love are with his family and friends at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Danny.”.

A tribute feature has been included in Spurs’ matchday programme, while members of Kelly’s family have been invited to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, with the club planning to pay tribute to him at half-time.

Kelly’s family have also organised a round of applause in the 69th minute to mark his age.

Spurs’ head of communications, Anthony Marshall, opened Roberto De Zerbi’s pre-match press conference at Hotspur Way on Friday afternoon by offering condolences and confirming the club’s plans to celebrate Kelly.

“On behalf of everyone at Tottenham, I want to offer our condolences and love to the family, friends and colleagues of Danny Kelly, as well as everyone who read his work or listened to him on the radio,” Marshall said.

'F*** the Pope and the IRA' chant lands England in hot water as fans are given suspended one-game stadium ban and FA fined

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:19 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • UEFA have slapped the FA with a £12,500 fine and a suspended one-match away supporters ban after England fans were heard singing sectarian chants during their Nations League victory over Spain last weekend.
  • Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 13:19 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

UEFA have slapped the FA with a £12,500 fine and a suspended one-match away supporters ban after England fans were heard singing sectarian chants during their Nations League victory over Spain last weekend.

Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.

As a result, UEFA have fined the FA and banned away fans from attending one UEFA match for 'racist and/or discriminatory behaviour'.

That said, the ban will only take effect if England supporters reoffend within the next two years.

It is a fortunate reprieve given the Three Lions' next away fixture is their Nations League quarter-final, the draw for which is on Friday.

Meanwhile, the FA have committed to identifying those involved and taking action - which could see football banning orders imposed.

In a statement to Daily Mail Sport, the FA said: 'We will not tolerate this unacceptable and deeply offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action.'.

England fans land FA in hot water over 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' chant during Spain victory.

England supporters have notoriously sung the anti-Catholic and loyalist chant. In 2024, the Irish police urged travelling fans to 'respect local culture' before their Nations League match against the Republic of Ireland.

Fans were also filmed in Milan city centre on the eve of the clash against Italy in 2022 singing the same incendiary chant - just one year after their European Championship final defeat to the Italians.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, then England boss Roy Hodgson and the FA were forced to condemn supporters after the inflammatory chant was heard throughout England's 3-1 friendly victory over Scotland at Celtic Park in 2014. Around 5,000 fans travelled to the devoutly Catholic club.

Industry observers note that the problem is not limited to international football. In August, Daily Mail Sport revealed that Chelsea wrote to supporters after a section of their fans were heard singing the sectarian chant away at Fulham on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

England boss Thomas Tuchel was asked about racism in his pre-Spain press conference.

'I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on Earth and that's exactly how it works,' Tuchel remarked.

Recent findings suggest that 'I expect emotional and of course supporting fans from Spain for their national team. That's what I expect, but I don't expect racism nowhere.

'I'm shocked if it happens, and it should happen nowhere, and I'm the first one to stand up for these kind of values.

'My trust is that we have a friendly atmosphere, that we have an atmosphere who is clearly in favour of the Spanish team, and that football does what it does best: bring people together and not divide people.'.

Manchester United dealt setback after targeting Nico Paz transfer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have been dealt a blow in their pursuit of Nico Paz as Real Madrid intend to activate their €80 million (£67m) buyback clause to sign the midfielder from Como, according to reports in Spain.
  • Paz joined Como from Madrid two years ago and has established himself as the talisman in Cesc Fabregas’ side.
  • So far this season, the 22-year-old has been one of the standout performers in the Champions League, scoring three goals and registering five assists in four games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have been dealt a blow in their pursuit of Nico Paz as Real Madrid intend to activate their €80 million (£67m) buyback clause to sign the midfielder from Como, according to reports in Spain.

Paz joined Como from Madrid two years ago and has established himself as the talisman in Cesc Fabregas’ side.

So far this season, the 22-year-old has been one of the standout performers in the Champions League, scoring three goals and registering five assists in four games.

That included a man-of-the-match display in Como’s 4-1 win over United last month while piled more pressure on Michael Carrick.

Last week, reports claimed that United had identified Paz as a potential successor to Bruno Fernandes and were considering a move for the Argentina international next summer.

However, Cadena SER reports that Madrid are ‘determined’ to re-sign Paz at the end of the season and are planning to trigger the €80m (£67m) buyback clause which is part of their agreement with Como.

Madrid had the option to re-sign Paz this year but the midfielder personally requested to stay at Como for another season.

According to recent reports, ‘I thought this was where I would grow the most. I think I made the right decision and I’m happy I did,’ Paz stated in September.

Como spent €60m (£51.77m) on their deal to keep Paz at the club but Madrid, crucially, insisted that a buyout clause would remain part of their agreement.

Bukayo Saka will be sidelined for another four weeks while Arsenal will also be without Martin Zubimendi for their Premier League game against Newcastle United on Saturday.

Saka has missed Arsenal’s last five games after suffering a thigh injury during Arsenal’s 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League on October 21.

Recent findings suggest that when asked about the progress of Saka’s recovery, Arteta noted on Friday: ‘We had another test. He’s evolving really well.

Meanwhile, Zubimendi was forced off during Spain’s 3-2 defeat to England on Sunday and will miss Arsenal’s trip to St James’ Park this weekend.

‘He’s out,’ Arteta said of Zubimendi.

Emi Martinez has reclaimed his place between the sticks as Chelsea host Leeds today.

The Blues return to action at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon and Xabi Alonso was pondering whether to use Mike Penders or the fit-again Martinez.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan will hold their penultimate training session today in view of Sunday’s return to Serie A action with a game against Frosinone.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) writes that the Milan squad will return to full strength with the arrival of the final players returning from international duty, allowing Ruben Amorim to begin detailed preparations for Sunday’s 18:00 CET clash against Frosinone at San Siro.

Sources indicate that mike Maignan is expected to start in goal. He took part in a portion of yesterday’s training session alongside the other goalkeepers. The Frenchman’s recovery is progressing well, and Pietro Terracciano – who has been out for about 40 days with a shoulder issue – could make the bench.

It has been revealed that strahinja Pavlovic also participated in part of the group training and will be included in the squad for the match against the Ciociari. However, the Serbian defender is not yet at 100%, so unless his condition improves swiftly, he is likely to start on the bench.

Sankhoun Diawara would thus take the left centre-back spot, with either Davide Bartesaghi or Pervis Estupinan covering the left flank. The defence will be completed by Koni De Winter and Mario Gila, with the Spaniard operating on the right again.

In midfield, Yunus Musah, Luka Modric and Adrian Rabiot – who could play in a more advanced, attacking-midfield role – are expected to be the starting trio. In attack, Diego Moreira and Goncalo Ramos are guaranteed starters, with Christian Pulisic presently favoured over Alphadjo Cisse.

Predicted Milan XI (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric; Pulisic, Rabiot, Moreira; Ramos.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis, Schmid, Kvernadze; Birligea.

  • Kasimpasa will be looking to extend their unbeaten run when they welcome Alanyaspor to Recep Tayyip Erdogan Stadium on Sunday afternoon.
  • The hosts occupy fifth place in the Turkish Super Lig standings with 20 points from 11 matches, while the visitors sit 13th with 12 points and will be desperate to end a difficult run of results after losing their last four games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 21:38, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:43.

Kasimpasa will be looking to extend their unbeaten run when they welcome Alanyaspor to Recep Tayyip Erdogan Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts occupy fifth place in the Turkish Super Lig standings with 20 points from 11 matches, while the visitors sit 13th with 12 points and will be desperate to end a difficult run of results after losing their last four games.

Emre Belozoglu's sudden departure to Fenerbahce has not affected Kasimpasa, who have continued their encouraging run of form in recent weeks, putting together a five-match unbeaten streak in all competitions to move into contention for a place in the upper half of the Turkish Super Lig table.

The run began with a 4-1 home victory over Samsunspor, before they followed that result with a 1-0 away win against Eyupspor six days later.

They continued their progress with a 3-1 victory over Corluspor 1947 in the Turkish Cup, although their next league assignment proved considerably more challenging as they held Besiktas to a 2-2 draw at home.

Kasimpasa then produced another impressive performance in their most recent league outing, which was Alfred Schreuder's first game in charge, recording a 2-0 away victory over Gaziantep to make it three wins and a draw in their last four league matches.

The Apaches will therefore be confident of continuing their progress against Alanyaspor, particularly as they have yet to lose at home this season, although they have recorded just one victory, with the other four league games ending in draws.

The hosts will also draw encouragement from their recent record in this fixture, having avoided defeat in their last nine meetings with the visitors, winning seven and drawing two, including each of the last five encounters.

Alanyaspor, meanwhile, have endured a difficult period after making a reasonably encouraging start to the campaign, with their recent defeats leaving them in the bottom half of the standings.

Joao Pereira's side began their latest run of league fixtures with a goalless draw against Erzurumspor before suffering a 3-0 defeat away to Fenerbahce seven days later.

They subsequently lost 2-1 at home to Kocaelispor, with their defensive problems becoming more pronounced when they travelled to face Genclerbirligi, where they were beaten 5-0, suffering their heaviest defeat of the campaign.

Their struggles continued in their most recent league fixture, as they lost 2-0 at home to Trabzonspor, leaving them without a league goal in consecutive matches.

Their 4-1 Turkish Cup victory over 12 Bingolspor offered some encouragement between those league defeats, but the visitors have struggled to transfer that attacking performance into their domestic campaign.

Alanyaspor Turkish Super Lig form:.

Alanyaspor form (all competitions):.

Kasimpasa will be without Elson Mendes, who is suspended for Sunday's encounter, while Godfried Frimpong and Kamil Corekci are also expected to miss out through injury.

Kevin Mouanga, Fousseni Diabate and Mortadha Ben Ouanes are among the players carrying fitness concerns, while Andri Fannar Baldursson is also expected to be unavailable after picking up a muscle injury.

Adrian Benedyczak is expected to lead the attack after establishing himself as the club's leading scorer, with Haris Hajradinovic and John-Jules Rak-Sakyi likely to provide support from behind the striker.

Alanyaspor are expected to be without Paolo Fernandes, who is recovering from a muscle injury, while Fatih Aksoy is also a doubt after picking up an injury.

Pereira could therefore retain much of the side that started against Trabzonspor, with Ruan, Hwang Ui-jo and Ogulcan Usluoglu expected to provide the attacking threat for the visitors.

Kasimpasa possible starting lineup:.

Gianniotis; Winck, Arous, Ilie, Karapo; Jessen, Demirbay; Rak-Sakyi, Hajradinovic, Kol; Benedyczak.

Alanyaspor possible starting lineup:.

Paulo Victor; Nuno Lima, Aliti, Ozyurt; Hadergjonaj, Gezek, Maestro, Ozdemir; Ruan, Hwang, Usluoglu.

Kasimpasa have shown considerably more consistency than their opponents in recent weeks and have also dominated this fixture in recent seasons, which is why we expect the hosts to secure a comfortable home victory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alan Shearer is back with his latest predictions as Premier League action resumes after the international break.

The majority of the eyeballs will be on Anfield, where Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first Manchester United after replacing Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils are winless in their last eight games, but will hope that their newly introduced head coach can inspire them to a famous win against their arch-rivals Liverpool.

Elsewhere, Chelsea and Manchester City will look to get back to winning ways after defeats before the international break, while Thomas Frank begins life at Crystal Palace with a trip to Coventry.

As ever, England legend and Betfair ambassador Alan Shearer has revealed his Premier League predictions to Metro.

It has been revealed that I think City will get back on track here. I know it’s sometimes difficult after international breaks, but I saw Fulham against Newcastle and they deserved the point. But I think City will be too strong for them to get back to winning ways, and they need to get back to winning ways here.

Alan’s Prediction: Man City Win.

Chelsea Under-21s captain Olutayo Subuloye has been named to the bench for this afternoon’s Premier League meeting with Leeds.

He was an unused substitute for the Carabao Cup defeat by Liverpool, and will hope to make his debut at Stamford Bridge this afternoon.

He first joined Chelsea from Brighton at U12 level and was converted from a midfielder into a versatile centre-back, winning plenty of silverware in the youth ranks and signing his first professional contract at Stamford Bridge in 2024 that is valid until the summer of 2030.

Subuloye was one of the youngsters included in Alonso’s squad for their pre-season tour of Australia and Asia over the summer, but has yet to make his competitive debut for Chelsea.

Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli is also part of the group to have made the trip to Merseyside, with the 16-year-old midfield sensation looking to build his first-team experience after becoming Chelsea’s youngest-ever Premier League player when he came off the bench late on during last month’s 3-0 defeat by west London rivals Brentford.

There could also be a debut in store against Liverpool for summer signing Emmanuel Emegha, who has yet to make a single competitive appearance for Chelsea since joining from BlueCo sister club Strasbourg on a pre-agreed deal in July.

The Dutch striker scored in back-to-back behind-closed-doors friendlies against EFL opponents Crawley and Bromley during pre-season, but sustained a hamstring injury against the latter and has not featured since.

He was part of the squad for the Carabao Cup second round win over Luton back in August but did not play, while his long wait for a Chelsea debut has since been exacerbated by a setback suffered in training.

However, Alonso confirmed that Emegha would be available to face Liverpool and he has indeed made the trip as he looks to prove himself a worthy alternative to star forward Joao Pedro, who will miss the next few weeks with a thigh injury sustained before Saturday’s home loss to Tottenham in the Premier League.

Luca Williams-Barnett starts for Tottenham against Ipswich today.

Destiny Udogie, Savio, James Maddison and Lucas Bergvall were all pictured training at Hotspur Way this week and are now in contention for minutes on Saturday.

Udogie was left out of Roberto De Zerbi’s squad as Spurs lost 1-0 to Leeds before the international break, though the Italian left-back took to social media to suggest that he was not injured.

De Zerbi had previously said that Udogie’s injuries were becoming “problematic”, with the 23-year-old starting just two league games this season. He has slotted back into the starting lineup this afternoon.

Savio, meanwhile, is in line to return to action for the first time since October’s 1-1 draw with Manchester United. The Brazilian winger has missed Tottenham’s last four league games with a muscular issue and is on the bench.

It has been revealed that spurs sorely lacked a creative threat against Leeds. But despite naming Maddison on the bench at Elland Road, De Zerbi didn't bring him on in search of a goal, raising concerns about his fitness.

Maddison has struggled to train consistently since the start of the season and came off midway through Spurs’ 2-0 win over Chelsea with a suspected groin problem.

The 29-year-old has not featured since that historic victory at Stamford Bridge, despite being available for selection. After working on his fitness throughout the international break, he returns to the starting lineup here.

Mathys Tel is expected to be out for up to three weeks with an Achilles injury sustained following a heavy tackle from Leeds defender Jayden Bogle.

There is a fresh injury concern for De Zerbi, though, as Sandro Tonali has missed out on the matchday squad altogether, with the reason for his absence presently unconfirmed.

Mauricio Pochettino has arrived at Old Trafford tasked with lifting the club from their latest malaise and will be backed in January with a defender and a striker needed.

Bassey has emerged as a target at the back with United’s defence in disarray this season, conceding 19 goals in 10 appearances.

Fulham have no intention of selling the former Rangers star with Arbeloa describing him as one of the best defenders ‘in the world’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 21:40, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:42.
  • Konyaspor will be looking to halt their recent slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Besiktas to Medas Konya Buyuksehir Stadyumu on Sunday afternoon.
  • The hosts sit 15th in the table with eight points from 11 matches, only outside the bottom three on goal difference, while the Black Eagles occupy fifth place with 19 points from 10 games and will be hoping to maintain their push towards the top of the standings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 21:40, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:42.

Konyaspor will be looking to halt their recent slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Besiktas to Medas Konya Buyuksehir Stadyumu on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts sit 15th in the table with eight points from 11 matches, only outside the bottom three on goal difference, while the Black Eagles occupy fifth place with 19 points from 10 games and will be hoping to maintain their push towards the top of the standings.

Konyaspor have endured a difficult run of results in recent weeks, winning just once in their last six league matches and struggling to find consistency in the final third.

Ilhan Palut's side began that sequence with consecutive goalless draws against Kasimpasa and Istanbul Basaksehir before suffering a 1-0 defeat away to Amed SK.

They then recorded a 2-0 home victory over Genclerbirligi, but that proved to be their only success during the period as they suffered consecutive defeats against Galatasaray (4-0) and Samsunspor (1-0).

Konyaspor were particularly disappointing in their defeat away to Samsunspor just before the break, failing to take anything from a match against a side sitting second-bottom and enduring a losing run.

The result further highlighted their struggles in front of goal, with the hosts having scored just six times in their opening 11 league matches, an average of fewer than one per game, while they have failed to find the net in seven of those fixtures.

Konyaspor have scored four of their six goals and collected seven of their eight points on home soil, although they were thrashed by Galatasaray in their last home game and now face a Besiktas side that have beaten them in their last two league meetings.

The hosts did manage to defeat the Black Eagles 1-0 in their most recent encounter, although that victory came in the Turkish Cup.

Besiktas, meanwhile, have enjoyed a more productive campaign, collecting seven wins, one draw and three defeats from their opening 11 league matches to remain within reach of the leading teams, sitting six points behind league leaders Galatasaray.

Vincenzo Italiano's side are also unbeaten in their last three league games, a sequence that began with a 2-0 home victory over Istanbul Basaksehir before they were held to a 2-2 draw by Kasimpasa.

Their subsequent European fixture saw them suffer a 3-2 defeat against Celtic, but they responded positively three days later by recording a convincing 3-0 home win over Genclerbirligi.

Dusan Vlahovic was particularly influential in that victory, scoring twice as the Black Eagles returned to winning ways in the Super Lig and demonstrated the attacking quality that has made them one of the more productive sides in the division, with only four teams scoring more than their 23 goals.

However, the visitors have struggled on the road, winning just one of their five away league matches and failing to win any of their last three, during which they have recorded one draw and two defeats.

Besiktas Turkish Super Lig form:.

Konyaspor will be without Adil Demirbag, who is recovering from a cruciate ligament injury and is expected to remain sidelined for the rest of the season.

Chidozie Awaziem is also unlikely to feature after sustaining a muscle injury, while Marko Jevtovic is working towards regaining full fitness and faces a late assessment.

Ugurcan Yazgili is another concern after picking up a hamstring problem, leaving Palut with defensive and midfield decisions to make.

Mostafa Mohamed, Diogo Goncalves and Ebrima Colley are among the attacking options available to the Konyaspor manager, although Enis Bardhi is expected to miss out through suspension.

Besiktas will be without Umit Akdag, who is recovering from a broken wrist, while Fabio Miretti is also expected to miss the match with a shoulder injury.

Emmanuel Agbadou is not expected to return until later in December as he continues his recovery from a knee problem, while Orkun Kokcu is also sidelined with a foot injury.

Konyaspor possible starting lineup:.

Gungordu; Andzouana, Baniya, Bosluk, Masuaku; Toth, Ibrahimoglu; Colley, Goncalves, Dompe; Mohamed.

Besiktas possible starting lineup:.

Nubel; Murillo, Taylan Bulut, Topcu, R Yilmaz; Ndidi; Trossard, S Ozcan, Olaitan, Fakili; Vlahovic.

Konyaspor have struggled to produce consistent attacking performances this season, and although Besiktas have been inconsistent on the road, their attacking quality should be enough to overcome the hosts' defensive resistance, with Italiano's side expected to secure a comfortable victory in Konya.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

It has been revealed that ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps.

It has been revealed that following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

At the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he said. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”.

One expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

Industry observers note that “Availability,” he remarked, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of England vs Czech Republic from Wembley in the fourth and mercifully final round of fixtures in this sprawling Nations League international break. Tonight Harry Kane will win his 125th cap and equal Peter Shilton for England appearances.

It has been revealed that shilton’s took him 20 years as Gordon Banks was simply too good in the couple of years following his debut and then a couple of managers, Don Revie and Ron Greenwood, preferred Ray Clemence until the latter finally plumped for Shilton as No 1 in 1979. Kane’s, by contrast, have taken him 11. In that time he has been rested for a handful of friendlies but has not been unused in a competitive match when fit since Gareth Southgate left him out of the 5-0 victory over Sam Marino in 2021’s World Cup qualifier when Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored two and Ollie Watkins one goal on his debut.

England played the Czech Republic a week ago, winning 2-0 in Prague by virtue of Anthony Gordon’s cute header and Kane’s clever shot through a defender’s legs but they huffed and puffed for ages against a team harshly reduced to 10 men until they blew the house down. They went on to marmalise Croatia 7-0 in their next game in front of a crowd that sounded like a cross between the choirs on Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2 and There’s No One Quite Like Grandma.

In the past England have had problems backing up their best performances – the 4-1 evisceration of the Dutch at Euro 96 was followed by the cagey display in the quarter-final against Spain before prevailing on penalties, the 5-1 victory in Munich in 2001 led to a drab 2-0 win against Albania at St James’ Park the following Tuesday, in 2016 they went to Berlin and beat world champions Germany but were thumped by Netherlands, who had not even qualified for Euro 2016, a couple of days later. Even their thrilling, second-half showing against Croatia in their World Cup opener in June preceded the dreary 0-0 draw with Ghana.

Given the attacking fluency in Rijeka, Thomas Tuchel must be tempted not to to ring the changes and replace seven or eight players. He will have to find replacements for the injured Alex Scott and Ezri Konsa, however, and Calvert Lewin, who has had seven minutes of action, Rio Ngumoha 19, Morgan Gibbs-White 27 and Jarrad Branthwaite one, may feel they deserve a fairer opportunity to show what they can do in a match.
